req.title: Update existing post
req.statement: The system shall update the row when POST /<id>/update is called by the post's author with a title and body, and redirect to /.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /<id>/update by the post's author with a valid title and body must update the DB row and return a 302 redirect to /. I designed: (1) a positive EP test confirming the happy path — correct author, valid title+body → 302 to /, DB row updated; (2) a negative NEG test where a non-author (user 'other') attempts to update user 1's post → 403; (3) a boundary BVA test where title is an empty string → no redirect, error message shown (title required); (4) a DT test covering the unauthenticated case → redirect to /auth/login; (5) a STC test verifying the DB state transition — title and body are actually changed in the database after a successful update. Each test uses exact-value assertions to kill operator-flip and constant-bump mutations.

tests.name: test_update_post_happy_path_redirects_to_index
preconditions: DB contains post id=1 authored by user id=1 (username='test')
User 'test' is logged in via session
actions: POST /1/update with title='updated title', body='updated body'
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_post_happy_path_redirects_to_index():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/1/update', data={'title': 'updated title', 'body': 'updated body'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

test_update_post_happy_path_redirects_to_index()

tests.name: test_update_post_db_row_actually_changed
preconditions: DB contains post id=1 with title='test title', body='test\nbody'
actions: POST /1/update with title='new title', body='new body'
Query DB directly for post id=1
expected: State transition: old title 'test title' no longer present
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_post_db_row_actually_changed():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    r = client.post('/1/update', data={'title': 'new title', 'body': 'new body'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import get_db
        row = get_db().execute('SELECT title, body FROM post WHERE id = 1').fetchone()
        assert row['title'] == 'new title'
        assert row['body'] == 'new body'

test_update_post_db_row_actually_changed()
